cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: first year's depreciation of a $2,400 asset with a 10-year life
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as $480.00. Derived from the default double-declining factor of 2: 2400 * 2/10 = 480 for the first full period, which still exceeds the straight-line alternative so no switch occurs

cases.description: Documented example: depreciation between the 6th and 18th month of a 120-month life
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as $396.31. Independently derived by accumulating the double-declining amount month by month (rate 2/120), summing months 6 through 17 -> 396.30605

cases.description: Documented example: the same span with an explicit 1.5 declining-balance factor
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as $311.81. Same month-by-month accumulation with rate 1.5/120 -> 311.80894

cases.description: Documented example: a fractional end_period, where the period's depreciation is prorated
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as $315.00. The first period's depreciation at factor 1.5 is 2400*1.5/10 = 360, and 0.875 of that period is 360*0.875 = 315 exactly

cases.description: DIVERGENCE PROBE: no_switch TRUE suppresses the straight-line crossover in the late periods
cases.expected_note: Derived from the documented algorithm. Book values after three double-declining periods (rate 0.4) are 1000 -> 600 -> 360 -> 216. With no_switch TRUE periods 4 and 5 stay on declining balance: 216*0.4 = 86.4 and 129.6*0.4 = 51.84, totalling 138.24. With the default no_switch FALSE the same call switches to straight line and totals 216.00, so this case pins down whether the flag is honoured

cases.description: A negative life is outside the documented domain
cases.expected_note: DERIVED, not quoted: Microsoft's VDB page states 'All arguments except no_switch must be positive numbers' but does not name the error code. #NUM! is Excel's documented error for an out-of-domain argument across the rest of the depreciation family (DB, DDB, SLN, SYD all document #NUM! for a negative life), so #NUM! is what is asserted here
